note: A failed asset export now says why: `assetSummary.unavailable[]`, `failures[]` and the asset manifest carry `errorDetail` (the step, the time it took and what Figma or the transport said), where the plugin used to swallow the exception and leave only `DEVUP_ASSET_EXPORT_FAILED`. A layer inside an instance whose export fails is exported again after loading the file's pages - Figma's runtime refuses reads that need an unloaded page with "Unable to establish connection to Figma after 10 seconds", and an instance's layers are drawn from a main component on another page - and a recovered export carries `exportNote`; rebuild the plugin bundle to get it. Failures the plugin itself answered come back over the bridge in the remote `use_figma` shape, so they are classified as on the remote path (a missing node is `DEVUP_FIGMA_NODE_NOT_FOUND`, -32602) instead of all reading `DEVUP_FIGMA_DIRECT_UNAVAILABLE`, which had made Figma's page-load refusal look like a direct-path outage; a host relays the distinction with `scriptError`. `widthBehavior` marks roots drawn narrower than any screen (320px) `componentSized` and leaves out their `consumer-policy-required` findings (`summary.componentRootSuppressed`). `devup_runtime_audit` ingest returns `visualComparisons`, a ready `devup_visual_compare` call per screenshot taken at a drawn width with what the audit verified filled in and the rest named, and `devup_visual_compare` pins a reference given by `artifactId` itself (`environment.filledByServer`). Codegen no longer re-scans the source map per source-map entry when auditing generated attributes: a 790-node, three-width screen projects in 0.58 s instead of 15.3 s, with byte-identical output.
